en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Seventeenth Chapter
The Discourse on What is Bound by the Faculties.
Is that which is bound by the faculties itself suffering?
Yes, it is.

Is that which is bound up with the faculties impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, and subject to change?
You should not say so...

Is it not the case that what is not bound up with the faculties is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, and subject to change?
“Yes, [it is so].

“If that which is not bound to the faculties is impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, and subject to change, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘Only that which is bound to the faculties is suffering.’”
Is that which is not bound to the faculties, impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen,
and subject to change, not suffering?
Yes, it is.
Is that which is bound to the faculties, impermanent, conditioned, and subject to change, not suffering?
One should not say so... [and so on].
Is that which is bound to the faculties impermanent, conditioned,
and subject to change— and is it suffering?
Yes, it is.
Is that which is not bound to the faculties, impermanent, conditioned, and subject to change, also suffering?
You should not say so... [and so on].
Is suffering only that which is bound to the sense-faculties? Yes.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One that whatever is impermanent is suffering?
“Is that which is not bound by the faculties impermanent? Yes.
If so, then since it has been said by the Blessed One that whatever is impermanent is suffering—
“[That which is] not bound to the faculties is impermanent,” yet surely it should not be said that “only that which is bound to the faculties is suffering.
It should not be so stated.
“Is suffering indeed bound to the sense-faculties?”—
“Yes.

“Just as the holy life is lived under the Blessed One for the full understanding of suffering that is bound to the sense-faculties, is the holy life likewise lived under the Blessed One for the full understanding of suffering that is not bound to the sense-faculties?”

It should not be said so … [as before] … Just as suffering bound to the faculties, once fully understood, does not arise again, in the same way, suffering not bound to the faculties, once fully understood, does not arise again?
It should not be said so.
Therefore, suffering is indeed bound to the sense-faculties.
The discussion on being bound to the sense-faculties is concluded.
